chapter: Booker T. Washington Community Center Band
title: The beginners' teacher who forbade jazz
summary: Students practiced reading at home; the teacher rapped fingers of anyone who added jazz notes, yet the kids liked him, and older musicians resented that the band was training their replacements.

bands.name: Booker T. Washington Community Center Band

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: That's right. Well, would you -- would he send you all home to practice at home, reading?
Oh, yeah. You'd take your horn home and you'd practice.
And he gave you music books?

Yeah, you'd have your music book. You'd go home and practice you know, and run over it, so you could get it right when you came back. But he didn't allow you to play jazz. No, he didn't like you to play jazz. Anytime he caught you playing jazz he'd crack you on your fingers, you know.
Why? What did he tell you?

Well, he just said, 'No, don't play that. What is that? You don't see that on your music do you? So don't put that in there.' You know, some guys would slip in an extra note every now and then. Some guys had got smart, you know, had got out and heard somebody play or something, you know. And he'd come back and he'd try to slip it in, you know. And --
And he's say, 'That's not on the music,' huh?

Yeah. 'That's not on the music. Where do you see that? Don't put that in there. What are you doing?' And -- but we all liked him because he had little jokes, little sayings, he would carry on with us, and he was

a big, fine guy. They used to give him the devil because the older guys that was in that band, the older musicians, said, "They've only give him a stick to break your back," because those guys are going to come up some day and take your place, you know? Which they did. Which they did. They came out of there. It was like a turnover. You see, so many guys would leave, maybe, this year, because in the big band era it was, you know, so guys were looking for guys that could read, you know, band leaders like.
